name: Argos in Cappadocia
positioning: Sustainable cave and stone hotel laid out as a village-within-a-village in Uçhisar, overlooking Pigeon Valley
best_for: Travelers who want to sleep in historic cave interiors
Couples looking for a suite with its own private pool
Wine lovers interested in a cave cellar and chapel tastings

facts.text: Argos is in a small village in Uçhisar, overlooking Pigeon Valley with Erciyes Mountain beyond.
Argos describes itself as a sustainable hotel deeply connected to the land, its history and its culture.
Argos sits in the quiet village of Uçhisar, close enough to Göreme National Park and its attractions while keeping privacy from the tourist crowds.
Every room is different, combining traditional Cappadocia aesthetic with refined details.
The Splendid Suite has a private pool and a contemporary interior.
The spa's indoor pool has the same cavernous feel as the cave rooms.
The Argos Spa offers a signature massage that uses local healing herbs.
Nahita is a Gault-Millau gourmet restaurant whose seasonal menus revive forgotten flavors and recipes of Anatolia.
Around 22,000 local and international wines are stored in the hotel's cave wine cellar.
The hotel can guide guests to outside activities such as a sunrise hot air balloon ride or a hike or bike ride through the valleys.
Argos hosts intimate acoustic live music performances.
Event venues include ancient chapels and a Museum Hall with its own display of artifacts.

highlights.text: Argos is a village-within-a-village of terraces rising into the valley, with snaking paths leading to its rooms, pools, restaurants and gardens.
Rooms feature stone and/or historic cave interiors, depending on availability.
The Cave Splendid Suite pairs private pool access with a historic cave interior.
The heated outdoor pool is open all year-round and overlooks the entire valley.
Guests can join a wine tasting in the hotel's ancient chapel.

considerations.text: Some rooms are in interior sections of the hotel without windows, depending on availability.
WhataHotel notes the cave room layout may feel unconventional for some guests.
WhataHotel notes the remote location requires transportation planning.
